issue.title: Capture ! close exceeds the §12.7 70 ms budget at vault scale even before relation successors
issue.description:
## What is wrong

`docs/task-dependencies.md` §12.7 budgets a `!` / `x!` that closes a real prerequisite at
<= 70 ms, and the dependents pass at <= 5 ms added. The pre-relation implementation
already misses both at real vault scale. This was measured while landing bob-cli-fs.4.1
(capture relation successors), but that epic did not cause it: the misses below are on
the pre-feature baseline `8c7e7103`, or with relations disabled.

## Evidence

- Apollo, isolated scratch copy of `~/bob` (6848 .md files), release build of baseline
  `8c7e7103`, 25 interleaved dry runs (bob-cli-fs.4.1.6, recorded in §12.7): `!` Done
  median 219.87 ms (p95 271.89 ms). Adding the dependents pass costs +15.11 ms. `hello`
  is 32.23 ms.
- Athena (64 cores), scratch copy of `~/bob` (6846 .md files, 23.7 MB of Markdown),
  release build of master `b4a17e86` with an empty config (relations disabled), hyperfine
  with 5 warmups and 30 runs: `!capture-measure:implement` takes 95 ms mean, while `hello`
  takes 19 ms. Temporary timers placed inside that `!` path found the dependents byte pass
  (`SharedNoteBytes::build`) at about 11 ms and `plan_successors` at about 4 ms. About
  60 ms of the close therefore goes somewhere outside the dependents snapshot and successor
  planning: the catalog walk, settings reads, ledger retirement, restamping, output, or
  other work not yet attributed.

## Repro

Copy the vault to scratch (never the live vault) and write a fixture note
`capture-measure.md` containing `- [/] #task Send implementation prompt [id:: implement] ^implement`.
Use a day file `20261102.md` with `## Pomodoros` / `- [ ] () — BUILD` /
`  - [[capture-measure#^implement]]`. Then time
`bob capture -b <scratch> --dry-run --no-clip --no-ref -f json -- '!capture-measure:implement'`
with `BOB_DAY_FILE`, `BOB_NOW="2026-11-02 09:30:00"`, an empty `BOB_CONFIG_FILE`, and
isolated `XDG_*`. Follow the method recorded in §12.7.

## Scope

Profile the relation-disabled `!` close path, attribute the roughly 60 ms (athena) /
roughly 190 ms (apollo) above `hello`, and bring it toward the §12.7 budget, or record
the limitation honestly in §12.7. Keep the zero-read guarantees for `hello` and plain
`x`. Relation-specific overhead added by bob-cli-fs.4.1 is out of scope; that epic's
landing tale owns it.

task_type_fields.impact: Every managed Done from the CLI and Bob Mac Capture runs 3x over the documented interactive latency budget on apollo; the dependents pass adds +15 ms vs the 5 ms budget.
task_type_fields.repro: Release bob on a scratch vault copy (~6850 .md): time 'bob capture --dry-run -f json -- !capture-measure:implement' with an empty BOB_CONFIG_FILE; apollo baseline 8c7e7103 median 219.87 ms, athena 95 ms vs hello 19 ms (see description).

issue.creation_reason: Found while landing bob-cli-fs.4.1: the pre-feature baseline and the relations-disabled path already miss the documented !/x! latency and dependents-pass budgets, so this gap predates that epic and is not its work.

payload.description: Earlier fix removed eager whole-vault discovery from every capture; this is the remaining close-path latency.
Measured while landing this epic; its relation-specific overhead stays with the epic's landing tale.

payload.entry: NOTE-PULL LATENCY UPDATE (2026-11-04): On athena (Linux 6.12.113+deb13-amd64), the isolated 6,907-note Markdown copy measured 20 timed samples after one warm-up. Baseline from the bob-cli-gj.2.1 audit at b9fe9d0c: @sase p95 87.67 ms and @mac_inbox p95 63.98 ms. The release build at dad9e660, with working-tree changes included, measured @sase median 51.43 ms / p95 57.29 ms / max 61.65 ms and @mac_inbox median 19.35 ms / p95 21.26 ms / max 22.92 ms. Both note-pull routes meet the 70 ms p95 target. The !/x! Done path scoped to this bead was not measured by this run.

NOTE-PULL STAGE PROFILE (2026-11-04): At b9fe9d0c, the isolated-copy profile attributed about 19 ms to path collection and sort, 10 ms to per-path BTreeSet insertion in NoteIndex::from_paths, and 2 ms to basename diagnostics. The same cached-filename sort plus bulk-set implementation used here was measured at about 11 ms for NoteCatalog::walk in the optimization profile, reducing the path/index portion by about 18 ms. The old append_unconfigured_theme_warnings path loaded Catalog a second time for about 11 ms on every capture. The new path does not load Catalog when there are no configured themes or no daily component growth; when warnings are needed it reuses the batch catalog. Thus the second 11 ms load is eliminated on the benchmark no-growth paths. The release benchmark records the resulting end-to-end p95s: @sase 87.67 to 57.29 ms and @mac_inbox 63.98 to 21.26 ms, on athena, revision dad9e660. Stage-level after numbers are from the instrumented optimization profile for the identical walk algorithm; the no-growth warning branch structurally skips Catalog::load.
